juce::Timer Class Referenceabstract

## Detailed Description

Makes repeated callbacks to a virtual method at a specified time interval.

A [Timer](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1Timer.html "Makes repeated callbacks to a virtual method at a specified time interval.")'s [timerCallback()](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1Timer.html#acd7b5a020cd4979f9270dfc5a5634290 "The user-defined callback routine that actually gets called periodically.") method will be repeatedly called at a given interval. When you create a [Timer](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1Timer.html "Makes repeated callbacks to a virtual method at a specified time interval.") object, it will do nothing until the [startTimer()](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1Timer.html#acb43e06d5742106830080af3d50b422d "Starts the timer and sets the length of interval required.") method is called, which will cause the message thread to start making callbacks at the specified interval, until [stopTimer()](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1Timer.html#a2ff70b860a8c875658b4baa91c8bcef0 "Stops the timer.") is called or the object is deleted.

The time interval isn't guaranteed to be precise to any more than maybe 10-20ms, and the intervals may end up being much longer than requested if the system is busy. Because the callbacks are made by the main message thread, anything that blocks the message queue for a period of time will also prevent any timers from running until it can carry on.

If you need to have a single callback that is shared by multiple timers with different frequencies, then the [MultiTimer](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1MultiTimer.html "A type of timer class that can run multiple timers with different frequencies, all of which share a s...") class allows you to do that - its structure is very similar to the [Timer](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1Timer.html "Makes repeated callbacks to a virtual method at a specified time interval.") class, but contains multiple timers internally, each one identified by an ID number.

See also[HighResolutionTimer](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1HighResolutionTimer.html "A high-resolution periodic timer."), [MultiTimer](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1MultiTimer.html "A type of timer class that can run multiple timers with different frequencies, all of which share a s...")

juce::Timer Class Referenceabstract

Detailed Description

Makes repeated callbacks to a virtual method at a specified time interval.

A Timer's timerCallback() method will be repeatedly called at a given interval. When you create a Timer object, it will do nothing until the startTimer() method is called, which will cause the message thread to start making callbacks at the specified interval, until stopTimer() is called or the object is deleted.

The time interval isn't guaranteed to be precise to any more than maybe 10-20ms, and the intervals may end up being much longer than requested if the system is busy. Because the callbacks are made by the main message thread, anything that blocks the message queue for a period of time will also prevent any timers from running until it can carry on.

If you need to have a single callback that is shared by multiple timers with different frequencies, then the MultiTimer class allows you to do that - its structure is very similar to the Timer class, but contains multiple timers internally, each one identified by an ID number.

See also
HighResolutionTimer, MultiTimer
